To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the mRNA8 and 10 of mouse hepatitis virus (JHM strain) were observed at the early stage of viral replication cycle, suggesting that these mRNAs might play a role in virus replication in vivo.

two additional small RNAs are transcribed from the mouse hepatitis virus (strain JHM) and that the imperfect intergenetic sequence may serve as an initiator site for leader- primed transcription in vivo.

two additional small mRNAs were found in MHV-infected mouse DBTs cells, and that these two small RNAs were found to be transcribed in the liver and the brain of a mouse that was infected with the JHH strain of MHV.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the transcription of small mRNAS containing a leader sequence.
the transcription of small mRNAS in the early stage after MHV infection.
the in vivo and in vitro expression of small mRNAS in the JHM strain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
MHV strain JHM can utilize a perfectly conserved and an imperfectly consaved intergenic site to transcribe small mRNAs in vivo and in vitro.
the leader sequence of MHV can be used as a primer for transcription of small m-RNAs in vivo and in vitro.
the small mRNAS, mRNA8 and 8, are transcribed in vivo and in vitro, and that the imperfectly conserved sequences may serve as initiation sites for leader-priming transcription in vivo.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

1) The leader sequence of MHV is a functional promoter for the initiation of transcription in vivo; 2) The leader sequence is also a functional promoter for transcription in vitro; 3) The leader sequence contains an enhancer-like element for in vitro transcription; 4) The leader sequence may be used as a promoter to drive the expression of a reporter gene; 5) The leader sequence can be used to prime transcription of a reporter gene in vitro.
the leader sequence of MHV is a promoter for the transcription of small mRNAS, which are transcribed in the early stage and late stage of the viral infection in DBT cells.
the leader sequence of MHV is involved in the regulation of viral gene expression and may be a key factor in the pathogenicity of MHV.
The main takeaway from our work is that
leader-primed RNA synthesis is an important feature of the replication cycle of MHV, and it may also be a common feature of other coronaviruses.
the imperfect intergene sequence of MHV can serve as an initiation point for the leader-primed mRNA synthesis.
the leader-primed mRNA9 is a new member of the MHV family of small mRNas, and it can be initiated from an imperfect intergenic sequence in vitro and in vivo.
